newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia calls for China-Philippines dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia calls for China-Philippines dialogue.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas on Wednesday called on China and the Philippines to settle their differences over the Spratly Islands through dialogue.
"What has happened between China and the Philippines, I think supports our approach nowadays...these things need to be settled through dialogue," Alatas told reporters.
"If we do not develop such dialogues, I think the problem could worsen," he added.

A row between the Philippines and China over rival claims in the South China Sea intensified on Tuesday when Beijing protested at the seizure of 21 Chinese fishermen and their boats in the disputed area.
Alatas said there were channels for dialogue between China and the Philippines and that talks should be held as soon as possible.
The Spratly Islands in the South China Sea are a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, claimed wholly or in part by China, the Philippines, Vietnam, Taiwan, Malaysia and Brunei.
Indonesia does not lay claim to the Spratly chain but has been keen to play a mediating role between claimants.
